sources.entry: ai-manus — Self-hostable Manus-style agent with sandboxed Docker environments, Terminal/Browser/File/Search tools, MCP integration, and optional OpenClaw (Claw) integration for one-click deployment.

summary.one_liner: AI Manus is a self-hostable general-purpose AI agent system that runs terminal, browser, file and search tools inside per-task Docker sandboxes, with a web UI.
summary.what_it_does: Runs a plan-and-execute agent loop where the planner and executor submit structured results via native tool calls (such as create_plan and complete_step). Each task gets its own sandbox, an Ubuntu Docker container that the server creates through the Docker socket. Agents can call Shell, Browser, File, Search and MCP tools inside that sandbox. Users can watch the browser live over VNC/NoVNC and take over. The web UI supports stopping or interrupting runs, file upload and download, multi-session history, background tasks, and a Library of attachments and artifacts. The README also describes a Skills system (reusable skill packages loaded into the sandbox) and a Chinese/English interface. Sessions are stored in MongoDB and Redis, and login/authentication is included.
use_cases: run AI-driven code execution in isolated containers
automate browser tasks with an AI agent and watch it live
let an LLM use shell, file and web search tools safely
connect custom MCP tools to an agent
build a Manus-style agent on my own infrastructure
how_to_run: Save the provided docker-compose.yml (frontend, backend, sandbox, mongodb, redis services)
Copy .env.example to .env and set API_KEY (and optionally API_BASE and MODEL_NAME)
Ignore the 'sandbox-1 exited with code 0' message; it is expected
Open the browser at the frontend port (5173 in the example compose file)
stack: Chrome headless, xvfb, x11vnc, websockify, NoVNC
notable: Per-task Docker sandbox with Terminal, Browser, File, Search tools and live browser viewing with takeover
Structured output via native tool calling instead of JSON-in-prompt
Minimal deployment needs only an LLM service and Docker
Skills system with official catalog, uploads and GitHub import
Library aggregating attachments and artifacts across sessions
caveats: Requires Docker, and the backend needs access to /var/run/docker.sock
Needs an LLM with reliable native tool calling; README recommends DeepSeek and GPT models
Roadmap items (Deploy & Expose, mobile/Windows sandboxes, K8s/Docker Swarm) are not yet supported
